Break your goal down into milestones and steps to track your progress.
A selection of steps will help you choose a direction and plan a route.
They help you see what is really important and find inner support.
Understand what principles and roles drive you every day.
Write down 10–15 things that are important to you (family, creativity, freedom).
Group them by topic and note what is supporting you right now.
Choose three core values ​​and come up with one action for each.
Find out what skills give you energy and results.
Ask three people close to you to describe times when you were at your best.
Review recent successes and highlight recurring skills.
Formulate three points about your strengths and post them in a prominent place.
They help you choose priorities and see the next peak.
Draw a circle of eight sectors: health, relationships, career, etc.
Rate your satisfaction with each area on a scale of 0–10.
Select the three sectors with the lowest scores and formulate goals for 90 days.
Imagine what your ideal day looks like in five years.
Describe the morning, work and evening of your ideal day in detail.
Compare with current reality and find three inconsistencies.
Write down the first step that will reduce each discrepancy.
They help you maintain focus and not give up on what you started.
Create a planning cycle to make the movement visible.
Break your goal down into mini-tasks that can be completed within a week.
Write down the “done” criterion for each mini-task.
Schedule a weekly review and record your progress.
Connect people who will help you reach your goal.
Choose a mentor or reporting partner.
Agree on the format of calls or messages once a week.
Prepare questions that you will discuss during meetings.

We often see only mistakes and miss our strengths.\nThis section helps you regain balance and see yourself objectively.

When you write down your qualities, successes and good moments,\nyou create a personal source of support that is always at hand.\nIt gives strength on difficult days, and on ordinary days it helps you grow.

• achievements (even small ones)
• successes of the day
• character qualities
• moments when you coped with it
• situations when you showed kindness, courage, caring

✔ Our brain remembers negativity more strongly.
✔ A list of achievements restores confidence.
✔ Facts help cope with anxiety and doubts.
✔ You begin to see the good in yourself that you previously missed.
You\'re a lot tougher than you think. Let\'s record this.
